neighbours.label: ' on' as the particle of a phrasal verb of supplying or stinting (lay on, skimp on, scrimp on), vs ' on' as a plain locative preposition
fire: The village always knows how to lay on a great festival in June.
Don't skimp on the butter if you want the pastry to be flaky.
The hotel laid on a free bus to the station for every guest.
We had to scrimp on heating last winter to pay the rent.
Never skimp on safety gear when you work with power tools.
The school laid on extra lessons before the exams.
My parents would scrimp on clothes so we could go on holiday.
They really lay on a feast whenever relatives visit.
quiet: The village always holds a great festival in the square in June.
Put the butter on the table so it softens before baking.
The hotel ran a free bus to the station for every guest.
We had to cut heating costs last winter to pay the rent.
Always wear safety gear when you work with power tools.
The books were left on the desk before the exams.
My parents would save money so we could go on holiday.
The cat was sleeping on the sofa whenever relatives visit.

predictions: Phrasal 'lay on / skimp on / scrimp on' reaches 0.3-0.65; locative 'on the table' and rephrasings without the particle stay under 0.1.
